=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
  Line or code reference: The new `elif [ "${EDITOR_NOOP_RECOVERABLE_FAILURE:-false}" = "true" ]` branch in the "Telegram editor-noop-suspicious warning" step — specifically the `attempts_label="every"` default plus the `MSG="⚠️ Editor failed on ${attempts_label} attempts: #${PR_NUMBER}"` and `BODY="⚠️ **Editor no-op suspicious** — the editor failed on ${attempts_label} attempts and produced no output (recoverable failure), so no fix was applied this pass."` templates that interpolate it.
  Problem: When `editor_attempts` ends up as 0 (PREVIOUS_REVIEWS_DIR unset, directory missing, or no `editor_attempt_*.err` files), the `[ "${editor_attempts:-0}" -gt 0 ]` guard is false so `attempts_label` stays at its initial "every". The MSG template then renders as "Editor failed on every attempts: #PR" and the BODY template renders "the editor failed on every attempts and produced no output". "every" does not agree with the plural "attempts"; the natural reading is "every attempt" (or restructure so the count noun lives inside the variable).
  Why it fails at runtime: This branch fires whenever EDITOR_NOOP_RECOVERABLE_FAILURE=true AND no stderr files are available, which is reachable when PREVIOUS_REVIEWS_DIR is unset/empty or the directory lacks editor_attempt_*.err. In that degraded state the operator-facing Telegram warning and PR comment both carry the grammatically wrong "every attempts" wording alongside the "not captured — see the editor step log of the linked run" fallback. `test_noop_warning_step_branches_on_recoverable_failure_with_last_error` only exercises the 3-attempt happy path so the wording defect is not caught by the contract.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
  Line or code reference: line 7858, `"failure_class": "refusal" if bool_env("EDITOR_NOOP_REFUSAL") else "unexpected_noop"` in the REVIEW_AUTOFIX_RUN_SUMMARY_V1 builder
  Problem: A run that ends in the recoverable_failure partial-finalize summary is still classified as `unexpected_noop` in the machine-readable run summary — the same misattribution this PR fixes for the Telegram alert and PR comment. The PR incident motivation (PR #4077, 21 consecutive broker-429 runs) would still aggregate under `unexpected_noop` in this telemetry surface.
  Why it fails at runtime: The summary block reads flags from the step env; `EDITOR_NOOP_RECOVERABLE_FAILURE` is exported via GITHUB_ENV at line 4639 before this step runs, so `bool_env("EDITOR_NOOP_RECOVERABLE_FAILURE")` is available but never consulted. Every recoverable-failure run keeps emitting the wrong failure class to the log-analysis pipeline that consumes REVIEW_AUTOFIX_RUN_SUMMARY_V1.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 6795-6799 and 6810 — `attempts_label="every"` fallback interpolated as "Editor failed on ${attempts_label} attempts"
  Problem: When no `editor_attempt_*.err` files exist (the `cp ... || true` copies at review_apply_fixes.sh:2108/2123/2133/2423 are best-effort, and PREVIOUS_REVIEWS_DIR may be absent), `editor_attempts` stays 0 and the operator message reads "Editor failed on every attempts: #N" — grammatically broken wording in the user-facing alert this PR exists to improve. Also "all 1 attempts" when exactly one attempt ran.
  Why it fails at runtime: Deterministic string interpolation: the fallback label "every" composes with the hardcoded plural "attempts", producing incorrect English on exactly the degraded-evidence path where the alert matters most.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
